name: GreyVibe
iocPatterns: Malicious ZIP/RAR archives hosted on third‑party file sharing services
Fake CAPTCHA web pages mimicking security verification
Domain names impersonating Ukrainian government entities
WebRTC live call portals used for audio/video capture
Obfuscated loader scripts designed to conceal execution
keyCapabilities: Delivery of malware through third‑party file sharing services (Google Drive, 4sync)
Use of decoy pages and lure sites including fake CAPTCHA pages, adult‑club sites, and WebRTC live call portals
Custom obfuscation techniques (DAYLIGHT, SAWDUST/CRUDEDUST, PyInstaller, JavaScript loaders)
Generation of malware with generative AI/LLMs
Post‑compromise persistence tools such as WireGuard, ZAPiXDESK and custom watchdogs
Overlapping C2 infrastructure shared across campaigns
AI‑generated phishing lures and malicious imagery (Ideogram, ChatGPT, Gemini)
Android spyware FallSpy collecting contacts, call logs, device info, location and media
recommendedActions: Deploy advanced email filtering that blocks and scans malicious ZIP/RAR attachments
Block or monitor access to public file‑hosting services (Google Drive, 4sync) and suspicious domains
Provide targeted user education on phishing lures, fake CAPTCHA pages, and adult‑club front sites
Implement IDS/UEBA capable of detecting decoy site access patterns and unusual WebRTC usage
Monitor endpoints for obfuscated scripts or JavaScript execution outside normal application contexts
Detect and block unauthorized WebRTC session initiation from corporate networks
Segment the network to limit lateral movement post‑compromise and enforce least privilege
campaignsText: GreyVibe’s known campaigns date from August 2025 through early 2026, with a concentration on Ukrainian and European targets in high‑value sectors. The actor employs a consistent operational tempo: initial spear‑phishing via malicious archives followed by decoy site engagement before payload deployment. While definitive links to larger nation‑state networks remain uncertain, the overlapping C2 domains and shared post‑compromise tooling suggest collaboration or at least shared infrastructure with other Russian interest groups. Victims tend to be mid‑to‑large organizations (government agencies, defense contractors, media outlets) where credentialed access provides valuable intelligence. Notable operations include a multi‑day phishing wave that led to the compromise of several Ukrainian military logistics units and a separate incident involving Android spyware installation on pharmacy supply chain employees.
description: GreyVibe is a Russian-linked threat actor that leverages generative AI to create tailored phishing lures and obfuscated malware, primarily targeting Ukrainian and European entities in the government, defense, pharmaceutical, media, and energy sectors. The group uses spear‑phishing with malicious ZIP/RAR archives delivered via third‑party file sharing services and deploys decoy sites such as fake CAPTCHA pages and adult‑club fronts to facilitate initial access. Its operations include post‑compromise persistence tools and overlap in C2 infrastructure with other campaigns, indicating moderate sophistication and a focus on political objectives.
goals: GreyVibe appears driven by geopolitical objectives to undermine Ukrainian governmental and critical infrastructure while also pursuing financial exploitation. By combining politically themed phishing material with advanced A.I. assistance, the actor seeks to maximize click‑through rates and compromise key personnel, thereby enabling espionage or sabotage. The group’s focus on sectors crucial to national security—defense, energy, pharmaceutical—suggests an intent to inflict broad systemic damage or to create leverage points for extortion. Geographically, the threat prioritizes Ukraine while extending its reach into neighboring European states (Poland, Ukraine), leveraging cross‑border infrastructure and language familiarity. Their use of decoy sites that mimic Ukrainian government domains indicates deliberate local targeting designed to increase credibility with regional employees.
